Expanded research program · candidate areas

16-area evidence and coverage screen

Use the same OPERA DSWx-S1 collection, date window, and nominal 625 km² screening footprint across all candidates. Public planning and hazard evidence supports relevance; the study will not claim full validation until QA-valid scenes and independent labels are reviewed. CMR metadata audit found 0 exact acquisition dates shared by all 16 areas, with metadata in 24 common year-month periods; this supports event-relative matched-count sampling, not same-date comparison.

Evidence-based selection criteria: Candidates use a balanced 8+8 frame, equal nominal 625 km² AOIs, a common OPERA DSWx-S1 V1 metadata window, and location-specific public research/management evidence. We do not rank cities with an unapproved composite-value score. Current gates: 16/16 candidates have documented public-need context and complete metadata queries; the initial 2025 RTC draw passed 169/192 samples, then the coverage-conditioned matched quota selected 192/192 groups across 16/16 areas after screening 34 additional groups; 0/16 pass confirmatory enrollment. Metadata and news-derived event leads are discovery only. Confirmatory enrollment also requires event-specific QA-valid OPERA scenes, independent licensed labels, probability sampling, and the predeclared precision gate. Shared public-value framework · apply the same five steps in all 16 areas
  1. Hazard observation: report product class, acquisition time, valid-pixel fraction, and uncertainty.
  2. Asset exposure: intersect dated, sourced asset footprints and report overlap and geometry completeness.
  3. Service consequence: add criticality, population served, and dependencies only from attributable data reviewed with responsible agencies or communities.
  4. Distributional equity: report who is represented and where coverage is missing, using privacy-preserving, locally governed data.
  5. Decision usefulness: evaluate evidence against documented local priorities; use no weighted social-value score without stakeholder-approved weights and sensitivity analysis.

Keep observation, exposure, consequence, equity, and decision relevance separate. Water overlap alone does not establish damage, service failure, financial loss, realized benefit, or customer demand; unknowns stay unknown.

Archive metadata is not a downloaded observation. The 16 areas share 0 exact acquisition dates; 24 of 26 year-month periods represented have at least one metadata date in every area. This supports event-relative sampling, not same-date comparisons, and does not prove equivalent usable pixels. The 90-date metadata cutoff is discovery-only. Three QA-valid scenes per event/baseline period and 80% valid pixels per scene are feasibility floors, not evidence of adequate sampling. Confirmatory enrollment also requires independent event labels, a probability sample, and the predeclared precision gate below.

SpaceNet 8 · Hurricane Ida

New Orleans · 160 annotation tiles overlap

4,500 unique building/road references intersect the fixed box; 14 have source label flooded=yes. 4,486 null flood states remain unknown; the audit does not count them as dry. Labels were manually interpreted from pre/post high-resolution optical imagery. Flooded buildings mean water nearby; roads may be labeled for visible water or rubble. This is a sparse object-level event reference, not a pixel water mask, field truth, or confirmatory validation.

16-area evidence-readiness ledger

0/16 confirmatory sites eligible · 192/192 selected RTC groups meet the matched 80% quota (16/16 areas; 34 extra candidates screened)

The same fixed-area crosswalk lists metadata dates, 12 sampled VV availability groups, and each public reference lead for every U.S. and international candidate. The initial random availability draw passed 169/192; the separate matched quota conditions selection on the 80% coverage floor and is not an archive-wide pass-rate estimate. Mumbai’s two NRSC maps are separately flagged as official-use leads with unverified overlap and reuse terms. Jakarta also has a 2024 BPBD administrative incident extract (260 rows across four reporting periods); it has no coordinates or event-day timestamps, and its reuse license is unverified. These source counts have different meanings and do not establish comparable flood labels or adequate event/baseline sampling.

Event acquisition opportunities: the three top metadata-ranked Groundsource event leads for each of 16/16 areas have an OPERA metadata date within one calendar day and at least three metadata dates in each 30-day pre/post window. Calendar dates do not establish an exact 24-hour match; source events need official verification, and QA-valid pixels and independent labels remain unverified. News coverage is geographically uneven.

The common proposed sampling and measurement rules are summarized below and apply equally to all candidates.
Common quality and sampling contract

Shared validation protocol

Proposed design—not externally preregistered. The same measurement, reference, sampling, and precision rules apply to every candidate. The 90-date metadata count is discovery bookkeeping; three valid scenes and 80% scene validity are feasibility checks only.

Confirmatory enrollment: 0 / 16

Measurement

Use OPERA DSWx-S1 V1 at 30 m with BWTR for mapped surface water. Invalid masks and no-data are missing, never dry. Water class alone is not flood truth.

Independent events and labels

Select events from dated independent evidence before viewing product results. Use temporally matched references, two blinded labelers, adjudication, and documented lineage and license.

Probability sample and precision

For an overall accuracy/proportion estimate, plan 385 effective independent reference units per site-period (95% confidence, ±5 percentage points under simple random sampling). That is 12,320 area-period reference assessments across 16 areas and event/baseline periods before design-effect, nonresponse, and finite-population adjustments. Class-specific accuracy requires separate sample allocation.

Comparable 8+8 results

Keep equal 625 km² footprints, event-relative windows, matched observation counts, area-weighted metrics, and design-consistent uncertainty. These purposive sites do not support national or global city prevalence.

No candidate currently qualifies for confirmatory validation. If independent labels or the precision target are inadequate, report the area as exploratory with achieved precision; do not claim a completed 8+8 comparison.
